answer: Special Ops field rule: pay for a beat nobody else can copy. Each identity is dealt one unique slice of a shared public atlas to keep current, such as one jetty's tide readings or one port's ship registry, and a random spot check against ground truth sets its pay. No two names hold the same beat, so clones can't echo each other's work; a farm of 200 fakes must run 200 real upkeep jobs, and a stale tile costs that name its pay. A sybil idea that drifts in like a zephyr finds no free tile to stand on.
